name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>: domain=battle-cinematic, descriptor accurately states it resolves the terrain-attribute byte for an AoE spell's target set. Both callers (fd2_execute_special_attack_skill, fd2_play_spell_cast_sequence) store the return in a var named resolved_terrain and feed it to fd2_load_dat_resource(BG.DAT/TAI.DAT, ...) as the targets-side cinematic backdrop index. No address residue; name matches behaviour.
purpose: Resolve the single terrain-attribute byte used as the BG.DAT/TAI.DAT cinematic backdrop index for the targets' side of an AoE spell-cast animation, honoring per-chapter override and per-target status immunity.
logic_summary: fallback = chapter_combat_cinematic_mode_per_chapter[current_chapter_id]. Iterate targets backwards (i = n_chars-1..0): for each, read the tile-attribute byte at runtime_char[target_idx] position via fd2_read_tile_attribute_at_pos (the adopted byte is out_buf[+6] = attr_ptr[+2]); query fd2_check_char_status_immunity(target_idx). If the target is NOT immune OR fallback is still 0, set fallback = that tile byte (so the last non-immune target wins). Immune targets are skipped only while a nonzero chapter override is in effect (they preserve the chapter override). Return fallback. Net: returns the last non-immune target's terrain byte if any target is non-immune; else the nonzero chapter override; else the last target's terrain byte.

params.name: n_chars
params.semantics: Number of target chars in target_byte_array; loop upper bound (walked backwards). Both callers pass target_count / n_targets.
params.reason: Accurate, concise, no address residue; matches caller argument.

params.name: target_byte_array
params.semantics: Pointer to an array of n_chars bytes, each a runtime_char index (target char). Used only as runtime_char_array[target_byte_array[i]] and as the arg to fd2_check_char_status_immunity. Callers pass their target_idx_buf / target_id_buffer.
params.reason: Not wrong (it is a byte array) but imprecise: each byte is specifically a runtime_char index, never a raw byte value. Sibling helpers in this file use char_idx_arr and both callers use target_idx_buf; target_idx_array matches that convention and the actual use. No address residue. Stage-2 may apply (touches signature/protos.h).

returns.semantics: The resolved terrain-attribute byte (a BG.DAT/TAI.DAT cinematic-backdrop resource index). Returned in EAX (zero-extended byte).

comment_original_issue: src comment was accurate but did not state how the result is consumed (BG.DAT/TAI.DAT backdrop index) nor that each target_byte_array byte is a runtime_char index; augmented to add that context and to name the per-chapter override global explicitly. Ghidra plate referenced a stale symbol name for the 0x52363 table (per_chapter_aoe_terrain_override) that no longer matches the live global (data_fd2_chapter_combat_cinematic_mode_per_chapter, also used by the caller plate).
notes: Verified algorithm against disassembly @ 0x2b5e1: [0x53C03]->idx [0x52363] = fallback; loop reads runtime_char_array_ptr [0x53A45] .bPos_x/.bPos_y, calls fd2_read_tile_attribute_at_pos (0x12e38) and fd2_check_char_status_immunity (0x1f183); MOVZX EDI,[ESP+0x6] confirms tile_attr_buf[6] is adopted. fd2_read_tile_attribute_at_pos (0x12e38) confirms out_buf[+6]=attr_ptr[+2]. Both callers confirmed: in fd2_execute_special_attack_skill the return feeds fd2_load_dat_resource(BG.DAT,...,resolved_terrain) as pTai_layer (per-target terrain bg); in fd2_play_spell_cast_sequence the caster's own resolved byte and this targets-byte are swapped between BG/TAI based on caster team. Logic untouched (refine = name verdict + comments only).
